subject: Budget range validation — PayBridge monthly spend band
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paybridge.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-15T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Budget range validation — PayBridge monthly spend band

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can align the pricing/contract path with your procurement flow.

Key notes from the call:
- Expected steady-state token volume: you called out ~100–150M tokens/month in year-1 ramp, with an initial prod window of ~30–50M/month after the pilot.
- Planned model family: open weights SFT-style (we discussed the latency/cost tradeoffs).
- Internal economics target: Maya mentioned a target of roughly $100–$130 per 1M tokens (total delivered cost target).
- Procurement thresholds: you said anything under ~$25k/mo is fast-track; $25k–$75k requires procurement review; >$75k needs VP/legal sign-off and typically 4–6 weeks.

As next steps we need a quick validation from you on 3 points so I can finalize the quote and the internal pricing approval path:
1) Confirm expected monthly token band we should price for initially (choose one): PoC (10–20M), Pilot (30–50M), Prod (100–150M).
2) Confirm target $/1M tokens that procurement would expect to see in the commercial proposal (Maya mentioned ~$100–$130 — is $120/1M acceptable as a target?).
3) Any procurement cadence/PO timing constraints we should bake into the contract (e.g., SOW timing, auto-renewal, invoice net terms).

I attached a short pricing sheet (redwood_pricing_sheet_q1_2027.pdf) showing list vs. committed volume bands and an example committed discount at 100M+. For transparency, list price for the model we discussed is $250/1M tokens; with a 12-month committed band at 100M+/mo that can move closer to $80–$120/1M depending on commitment and deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated).

If you can confirm the three items above by EOD tomorrow, I’ll route a draft commercial term sheet to you and loop legal for any procurement needs. Happy to hop on a 20m follow-up if that’s easier.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: redwood_pricing_sheet_q1_2027.pdf
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paybridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-15T12:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Budget range validation — PayBridge monthly spend band

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the points from our side: 

1) Monthly band to price initially: Pilot (30–50M tokens/month). We expect to run the pilot for ~6–8 weeks, then ramp to Prod (100–150M) over the next 6 months pending results.
2) Procurement target $/1M: yes — Maya and I are comfortable with a target of $120/1M for the initial pilot and will expect tiered reductions as we commit to sustained volumes. If you can show a committed price closer to $100/1M at 100M+ volumes that will make approvals smoother.
3) Procurement cadence: anything with an ARR or monthly spend below ~$25k can be handled by our procurement team in ~1 week. If the ARR/mth is between $25k–$75k it goes to procurement review (~2–3 weeks). Above $75k/month requires VP approval and legal review (~4–6 weeks). We prefer 30-day net invoices and an SOW that aligns to quarter boundaries.

Stakeholders to include on the commercial/PO loop: Maya Singh (CFO), procurement lead is Jake Carr (jake.carr@paybridge.com). I’ve cc’d Maya on this thread.

One other ask — can you include an appendix in the quote that maps model selection (hosted vs dedicated) to expected $/1M outcomes and any SLA implications? That will help our infra and security teams decide between hosted + private routing vs Dedicated.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Product, PayBridge
alex.johnson@paybridge.com
